Writing Portfolio

Your portfolio is a record of process and progress, not a folder of finished work. What it shows is how your writing changed — which is the thing this course is actually about.

The cycle

  1. Write→
  2. Get feedback→
  3. Revise→
  4. Reflect

You return to this cycle throughout the course. Each piece shows its journey: original draft → feedback → revised version → reflection.

The five pieces

🩺

Clinical Documentation

Objective, evidence-based documentation.

  • Accuracy
  • Objectivity
  • Concise writing
  • Professional language
📋

Patient Instructions

Clear, concise instructions a patient can follow.

  • Clarity
  • Organization
  • Plain language
  • Appropriate tone
✉️

Professional Email

A message to a member of the healthcare team.

  • Organization
  • Tone
  • Grammar
  • Workplace conventions
💡

Patient Education

A handout, FAQ, or similar patient-focused resource.

  • Health literacy
  • Word choice
  • Organization
  • Audience awareness
📄

Professional Letter

A formal letter for a realistic healthcare situation, such as a follow-up about a missed appointment.

  • Formatting
  • Tone
  • Organization
  • Professionalism

AI can suggest. You decide.

AI is a writing coach, not a replacement for your judgment. You may use AI to identify grammar or punctuation problems, suggest clearer wording, check organization, improve professional tone, flag confusing passages, and explain why a passage needs revision. You remain responsible for accuracy, professionalism, confidentiality, and final content.

When AI is the source of feedback on a portfolio piece, say so in your reflection, and say what you accepted and what you rejected. That judgment is the part that belongs to you.

I can…

Come back to this at the end of the course and see what changed.

I canWhich means
Write clearlyMy reader can understand my message.
Write accuratelyGrammar, spelling, punctuation, and information are correct.
Write objectivelyI distinguish facts and observations from opinions.
Write professionallyTone, organization, and format are appropriate.
Write for my audienceI adjust language for patients, coworkers, and other readers.
Revise my writingI can identify problems and make meaningful improvements.
